docs.text: On Thursday, NOAA’s GOESEast satellite captured this stunning visible imagery of severe thunderstorms bubbling near Chicago and sweeping over Lake Michigan. Wind gusts as high as 80 mph. Incredible imagery. Thanks NOAA!

NASA Satellite photo of the Great Lakes with Lake effect snow storm....Fantastic! You can see the outline of Lake Superior and Lake Michigan so well. Wow!!! #Photography #NASA #Astronomy #Earthscientists #Geography #Oneworld
Great satellite view of the Great Lakes today. My favorite tidbit is how you can see the elevation change through the lingering snowpack in southwestern Ontario.
The NOAA-20 satellite had clear skies last night and was able to capture a full image of the Great Lakes. Here it is overlaid with water temperatures (in Celsius).
From Lake Superior to the partially-ice-covered Lake Winnipeg, this satellite imagery showcases an enchanting view of lake effect clouds and snow streaming over parts of Canada and the US today.
Beautiful satellite imagery today. Kind of unusual to have so much clear sky over a fresh stripe of snow. Also included: another recent stripe of snow from Kansas to the Great Lakes. #uswx
Satellite image thanks to NASA and NWS of the Great Lakes on 1-21-25 showing lake effect snow.
So figured how to turn Satellite layers into workable KMZ's for our graphics system. So that is cool! This is from the NASA Suomi NPP today showing the Great Lakes around WNY!

"Great" day for a "Great" Lakes Satellite Loop. Mainly clear and cold, but able to see snow cover, frozen smaller lakes, G. Lakes ice and clouds whizzing by. #onwx #onstorm Thanks! GOES 19 VIS...you made my day🙂

Satellite capturing several distinct bands of snow accumulation (green stripes) from yesterday's extended lake effect snow band off Lake Ontario, including one across southern New Hampshire. Compared to the radar imagery from yesterday when that particular band was at peak intensity.
Snagged this from sat-20 a NOAA satellite shows the Great Lakes temperatures
The sun setting on an absolute beauty of a closed low over the Great Lakes. It's imagery like this that get me stoked for GOES-19 data to become more readily available.

Feb 26, 2014: Captured by NASA's Aqua satellite on Feb. 19, 2014, this false-color image shows the Great Lakes' significant ice coverage, peaking at 88.42%. Unusually cold temperatures contributed to this rare freeze-up. www.nasa.gov/image-article/ice-great-lakes-false-color-infrared
